messages.content: Good news: my husband’s vacation days are approved for July 19 through 24. Can we stop holding and book the Atlanta to Denver flights? I’m mainly worried about seats for the three of us, but I also don’t want to lock in the mountain hotel before I know more.

Yes, I’d move the flights from “hold” to “book now.” The Delta nonstops still match the family plan best: Saturday ATL-DEN without a connection, and the Thursday early-afternoon DEN-ATL return. The risk in waiting is less about the basic schedule and more about adjacent seats disappearing, especially on the Saturday outbound and Thursday return.
Is there any good reason to take the cheaper one-stop flights instead?

Only if the savings are large enough to justify a longer travel day. For this trip, the nonstop is cleaner: no connection risk, easier rental-car pickup, and a return time that does not eat the whole Thursday. The one-stop choices save money but add several hours and more chances for a delay. I would book the nonstop if the fare is still within the amount you were comfortable sending for approval.
Okay. Main Cabin, not Basic. For seats, three together if possible, but if not, one adult next to our child matters more than all three being in the same row.

Good seat rule. First choice: a full row of three together. Second choice: child plus one adult in a window/middle pair, with the other adult across the aisle or directly behind. I would avoid any layout where your child is not beside one of you. Choose seats immediately after ticketing, then recheck the map later because family seats sometimes open up after schedule or equipment adjustments.
Let’s put my kid at the window if we’re doing a pair. I can take the aisle across or behind if that’s the better arrangement.

That works. For the outbound, look first for child-window plus adult-middle, then place the other adult as close as possible. For the return, if a full row of three is still open, take it. If not, repeat the same paired setup. Since this is Main Cabin, standard seat selection should be available, but confirm before purchase so you are not stuck waiting for check-in.
Anything else I should watch for before I click purchase?

Check three things before purchase: fare class says Main Cabin, not Basic; carry-on and standard seat selection are included; and the change or cancellation terms are acceptable. If the checkout page offers a refundable upgrade, I would skip it unless the price difference is small, since the dates are now approved.
And hotels? Should I book Denver tonight too, or wait until we decide Estes?

I’d separate them. Book flights now. Then reserve a cancellable Denver hotel for July 19 to 21, because those first two nights are straightforward. For Estes Park July 21 to 24, do not take a prepaid mountain rate yet. Put a refundable hold on the leading option only after the room setup, parking, breakfast, fees, and cancellation terms are clear.
That makes sense. Denver can be cancellable. Estes is where I need answers before paying anything nonrefundable.

Tonight’s order: buy three Delta Main Cabin nonstop tickets ATL-DEN Saturday July 19 and DEN-ATL Thursday July 24 early afternoon; select seats right away with your child next to one adult and the other adult as close as possible; avoid Basic Economy and unnecessary prepaid add-ons. Then book only a cancellable Denver stay for July 19 to 21. For Estes July 21 to 24, wait on nonrefundable payment until you verify breakfast details, free parking, a suitable two-queen or family room, any fridge or kitchenette, total fees, and the cancellation deadline.

messages.content: Flights are ticketed. I got my kid a window on the outbound with one of us next to him, and we’re together on the way back. Can we settle the hotel pair now?

Great. For the split stay, I’d choose the pair that reduces friction on the actual days: downtown Denver for the first two nights, then the better-reviewed Estes Park lodge on a cancellable rate, with the simpler breakfast-included Estes property as the backup.
Can you compare them side by side? I’m trying not to overpay for a charming place if breakfast becomes a pain every morning.

Here’s the practical comparison. Denver downtown hotel: best for arrival weekend, walkable dinner, easier to enjoy Denver without driving after check-in, but breakfast is paid and parking will cost more. Quieter suite-style Denver option: more room and likely easier parking, but it is farther from restaurants and less convenient for the first evening. Estes better-reviewed lodge: stronger reviews and more of the mountain feel, but breakfast is not clearly listed and the room/parking details need confirmation. Estes simpler two-queen property: easier breakfast and parking, but less appealing overall for three nights.
For Denver, I do like the idea of being able to walk to dinner. We’ll have a car, but I don’t want to drive again after the flight.

Then the downtown Denver hotel is the better fit for July 19 to 21. The parking charge is annoying, but for only two nights it buys you easier evenings. Book the cancellable rate, request two queens, add a late-arrival note, and confirm the parking cost so it does not surprise you at checkout.
For Estes, is the higher-rated lodge enough better to risk breakfast not being included?

If it can confirm the basics, yes. For three nights near the park, room comfort, parking certainty, and overall guest experience matter a lot. Breakfast is useful, but I would not let it outweigh the better stay unless the lodge has no workable breakfast option nearby or cannot guarantee a room setup for the three of you.
Should I book both Estes places cancellable while I ask questions?

You can, but only if you set a reminder and the cancellation windows are clearly safe. Cleaner approach: place a refundable hold on the better-reviewed lodge first, ask the questions today, and keep the simpler breakfast-included property as a named backup. If rates are moving quickly, then holding both briefly is reasonable.
What exactly should I ask the lodge before I let that become the real booking?

Ask these before paying or letting a deadline pass: can they guarantee two queens or another comfortable setup for two adults and one child; is parking free, on-site, and available for late arrival; is breakfast included, paid, or unavailable, and what are the hours; is there a fridge, microwave, or coffee maker; are there resort or amenity fees; is there air conditioning; are there stairs or elevator issues; what is the exact cancellation deadline; and what is the full total with taxes and fees.
Okay, so downtown Denver plus the Estes lodge, both cancellable. Not the quieter Denver suite?

Correct. Book the downtown Denver hotel for July 19 to 21 on a cancellable rate because walkable dinner solves the arrival-night issue. Book or hold the better-reviewed Estes Park lodge for July 21 to 24 only if the rate is cancellable while you verify the room, parking, breakfast, and fees. Keep the simpler breakfast-included Estes property as the backup, not the lead, unless the lodge cannot confirm those basics.

messages.content: The Estes lodge replied. They can guarantee two queens and parking, but breakfast is only a paid grab-and-go. The simpler place includes breakfast, but recent comments mention hallway noise and smaller rooms. My husband is also asking whether one Boulder-area hotel for all five nights would be easier.

I’d keep the split stay. Boulder would reduce packing, but it makes the park days longer and more dependent on traffic and timed-entry windows. Since the Estes lodge confirmed two queens and parking, the main risk left is breakfast, and that is easier to solve than a noisy or cramped room for three nights.
So the one-hotel Boulder idea is not worth it?

Not for this itinerary. Boulder is a decent single base if you want a lighter city-and-mountains trip, but for RMNP days it adds too much backtracking. One hotel move is worth it because Estes puts you closer to the park and makes early starts less stressful.
And we accept the paid breakfast at the lodge?

Yes. Breakfast was one of the items to check, and it is not ideal that it is paid, but I would relax that point here because the lodge has the stronger room setup, confirmed parking, and better reviews. You can use the grab-and-go some mornings and do a grocery stop for fruit, bars, and kid snacks.
Which reservations should stay cancellable?

Keep both main reservations cancellable for now: downtown Denver until your arrival plan and parking cost feel settled, and the Estes lodge until the RMNP timed-entry plan and rental car are locked. I would not keep a Boulder hold unless your husband wants a 24-hour comparison. Cancel the simpler Estes backup once the lodge confirmation shows the exact total and cancellation deadline.
Can you give me the final hotel plan in one paragraph?

Final hotel plan: keep the split stay, with a cancellable downtown Denver hotel July 19 to 21 for easier arrival-night dinner and city time, then a cancellable Estes Park lodge July 21 to 24 because it confirmed two queens and parking and gives better RMNP access. Accept the paid grab-and-go breakfast and supplement with a grocery stop. Do not switch to a Boulder single base unless the park itinerary changes, and cancel the simpler Estes backup after the lodge total, fees, and cancellation deadline are confirmed.
